findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, which is stored in the instance metadata and Terraform state, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata service or state file.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data stored on the volume is unencrypted at rest, risking data exposure if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
The snapshot inherits encryption state from the unencrypted source volume, meaning the snapshot is also unencrypted, exposing potentially sensitive disk data at rest and to unauthorized sharing.

The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's administrative interface to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploitation attempts from any source.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, which is intended for a public web server but combined with the open SSH port and public subnet placement, increases the overall attack surface of the host.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to direct internet access when combined with the permissive security group.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, expanding the network's public attack surface unnecessarily.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to or tampering with sensitive network flow log data.
